```{r}
#| echo: false
capsule <- "results/reference/01_finemapping/separated-development-v1.1"
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(capsule, "benchmark_manifest.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE)
```

## Available benchmarks

### [Single-trait multichain convergence development benchmark](04_convergence/convergence-development-pilot.qmd)

| Status | Study type | Methods | Architectures | Chains | Maximum draws | Diagnostics | Capsule |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Complete one-replicate multichain development benchmark | Convergence | Matched ST BED/CSR BayesC and BayesR | Sparse homogeneous and sparse mixture | 4 per method (16 total) | 3,000 per chain | Rank-normalized split R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, relative MCSE, burn-in stability | [Capsule](../results/reference/04_convergence/st-multichain-convergence-development-v1/README.md) |

Passing operational thresholds supports provisional development settings for
these simulations; it is not universal proof of convergence.

### Single-trait parameter-estimation development benchmark

| Status | Study type | Methods | Architectures | Replicates | Primary estimands | Validation | Capsule |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Complete one-replicate development benchmark | Parameter estimation | ST BED/CSR BayesC and BayesR | Sparse homogeneous and sparse mixture | 1 | Effect, genetic and residual variance; heritability | 8/8 fits; simulation oracles passed | [Report](03_parameter_estimation/parameter-estimation-development-pilot.qmd) |

One replicate validates the reporting contract but does not establish bias or
interval calibration. A multi-replicate parameter-estimation benchmark with
convergence-informed MCMC and a separate single-trait multichain convergence
benchmark remain planned.

## Planned benchmarks

- Fine-mapping with realistic LD.
- High-LD causal architecture.
- Multi-replicate scientific-length prediction study.
- Single-trait parameter-estimation benchmark.
- Independent validation of convergence-informed MCMC settings.
- Multi-trait prediction study after computational optimization.
- Annotation-informed models.
- Block-eigen methods.
